title: Agentic Document Q&A System with Model Context Protocol (MCP)
summary: Multi-agent research and document intelligence platform where Planner, Retriever, and Synthesizer agents coordinate via MCP for fully grounded, verifiable Q&A over complex paper archives.
problem: Single-prompt RAG architectures struggle when processing dense technical literature and multi-document queries, often hallucinating citations or failing to recognize ambiguous user intents across disparate document collections.
approach: Built a modular multi-agent system governed by Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) standard. The architecture assigns distinct specialized agents: (1) Planner Agent decomposes complex multi-hop questions into focused sub-queries; (2) Retriever Agent interfaces with vector embeddings via MCP tool calls to fetch grounded chunk candidates; and (3) Answer Agent verifies context consistency, resolves conflicts, and generates synthesized responses with citation anchors.
architecture:
graph TD
    A[User Query] --> B[Planner Agent via MCP]
    B --> C{Query Sub-Decomposition}
    C --> D[Sub-Query 1: Core Methodology]
    C --> E[Sub-Query 2: Empirical Results]
    D & E --> F[Retriever Agent: Vector & Semantic Search]
    F --> G[Context Relevance & Cross-Check]
    G --> H[Answer Synthesis Agent]
    H --> I[Citation Verification & Faithfulness Check]
    I --> J[Final Structured Response Stream]
challengesAndLearnings: Ensuring deterministic state handoffs between MCP-connected agents required defining strict JSON Schema protocol contracts and implementing a consensus verification step before the synthesizer outputs final responses.

codeSnippet.code:
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
from langchain.chains import RetrievalQA

mcp = FastMCP("DocumentIntelligenceServer")

@mcp.tool()
async def retrieve_grounded_chunks(query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> list[dict]:
    """Fetches semantically relevant passages with source metadata and similarity scores."""
    results = await vector_store.asimilarity_search_with_score(query, k=top_k)
    return [
        {"text": doc.page_content, "source": doc.metadata.get("source"), "score": score}
        for doc, score in results if score >= 0.75
    ]

title: Ultra-Low Latency Conversational Voice Assistant
summary: Real-time bidirectional conversational AI voice agent featuring dynamic turn-detection and response streaming, cutting perceived end-to-end latency from 0.98s to 0.34s.
problem: Traditional conversational voice interfaces feel robotic and clunky due to multi-second delays between user speech pauses, speech-to-text transcript processing, LLM completion generation, and text-to-speech audio rendering.
approach: Engineered a low-latency streaming pipeline leveraging LiveKit WebRTC transport, Deepgram streaming Speech-to-Text (STT), OpenAI GPT-4o-mini with token-by-token streaming, and ElevenLabs WebSocket Text-to-Speech (TTS). Implemented dynamic Voice Activity Detection (VAD) and intelligent sentence boundary chunking to begin audio playback while downstream tokens are still generating.
architecture:
graph LR
    A[User Voice Input] --> B[LiveKit WebRTC Audio Stream]
    B --> C[Deepgram Streaming STT <100ms]
    C --> D[Dynamic VAD / Turn Detector]
    D --> E[GPT-4o-mini Streaming Tokens]
    E --> F[Sentence Buffer & Chunking]
    F --> G[ElevenLabs WebSocket TTS]
    G --> H[Audio Stream to User Headset <340ms]

metrics.label: Interruption Handling
metrics.delta: Instant audio cutoff on user barge-in

challengesAndLearnings: Handling natural user interruptions ('barge-in') without clipping required an asynchronous cancellation event bus that instantly drains the audio playback buffer and cancels in-flight LLM generations when user speech is detected.

codeSnippet.code:
async def stream_llm_to_voice(token_stream, tts_websocket, session_context):
    """Buffers tokens into phonetic clause chunks for immediate audio synthesis."""
    buffer = ""
    punctuation_delimiters = {".", "?", "!", ",", ";", ":"}
    
    async for token in token_stream:
        if session_context.interrupted.is_set():
            await tts_websocket.send_json({"action": "clear_buffer"})
            break
        buffer += token
        if any(p in token for p in punctuation_delimiters) and len(buffer.split()) >= 3:
            await tts_websocket.send_text(buffer.strip())
            buffer = ""

title: Enterprise Marketing & Sales Intelligence Agent in Snowflake
summary: Autonomous AI agent inside Snowflake data cloud combining Cortex Analyst and Cortex Search with Dynamic Tables, masking policies, and semantic layers for enterprise insights.
problem: Marketing and sales operations required hours of manual SQL writing and analyst support to combine structured CRM sales pipeline metrics with unstructured customer feedback and call transcripts.
approach: Built an automated in-database AI intelligence agent leveraging Snowflake Cortex AI. Configured Snowflake Dynamic Tables to automate incremental sentiment analysis and customer intent classification over raw logs. Defined an enterprise semantic data layer with column-level masking and RBAC security policies, allowing business users to ask natural language questions via Cortex Analyst and Cortex Search.
architecture:
graph TD
    A[Raw Sales & CRM Logs] --> B[Snowflake Ingestion Stage]
    B --> C[Dynamic Tables: Incremental ETL & Sentiment Scoring]
    C --> D[Enterprise Semantic Data Model & Masking Policies]
    D --> E[Cortex Search: Unstructured Feedback]
    D --> F[Cortex Analyst: Text-to-SQL & Aggregations]
    E & F --> G[Streamlit Executive Intelligence Dashboard]

metrics.delta: Down from 2-day manual analyst request backlog

codeSnippet.code:
-- Snowflake Dynamic Table with Cortex Sentiment Extraction
CREATE OR REPLACE DYNAMIC TABLE DT_MARKETING_SENTIMENT_ENRICHED
  TARGET_LAG = '10 MINUTES'
  WAREHOUSE = COMPUTE_WH
AS
SELECT 
    lead_id,
    account_name,
    feedback_text,
    SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SENTIMENT(feedback_text) AS sentiment_score,
    SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.CLASSIFY_TEXT(feedback_text, ['Churn Risk', 'Feature Request', 'Pricing Inquiry', 'Expansion']) AS intent_category,
    CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() AS processed_at
FROM RAW_CUSTOMER_INTERACTIONS;

title: Autonomous Multi-Agent Content Generation & Review Pipeline
summary: Collaborative multi-agent framework utilizing CrewAI and LLaMA 2 7B / GPT-4o to coordinate Planner, Writer, and Editor agents for automated, brand-consistent content production.
problem: Creating consistent, high-quality technical documentation and marketing briefs requires extensive cross-functional coordination, leading to editorial bottlenecks and brand voice divergence.
approach: Engineered a hierarchical multi-agent workflow with CrewAI. Defined autonomous personas: (1) Strategy Planner gathers market trends and structures the outline; (2) Content Writer drafts detailed copy incorporating technical depth; and (3) Senior Editor critiques the draft against brand voice, factual correctness, and SEO guidelines in an iterative critique loop.
architecture:
graph LR
    A[Content Brief / Topic] --> B[Planner Agent: Research & Outline]
    B --> C[Writer Agent: First Draft Creation]
    C --> D[Editor Agent: Compliance & Fact Checking]
    D -- Revisions Needed --> C
    D -- Approved --> E[Final Markdown & Social Formats]

metrics.label: Production Time Reduction
metrics.delta: From 6 hours to 15 minutes per brief

challengesAndLearnings: Preventing agents from getting trapped in endless circular revision loops by setting explicit max_iter thresholds and providing calibrated grading rubrics to the Editor agent.

codeSnippet.code:
from crewai import Agent, Task, Crew, Process

planner = Agent(
    role="Content Strategist",
    goal="Develop comprehensive research outlines for technical AI topics",
    backstory="Expert tech analyst skilled in synthesizing complex ML papers.",
    verbose=True
)

writer = Agent(
    role="Senior Technical Writer",
    goal="Draft engaging, accurate technical articles with code examples",
    backstory="Veteran developer advocate who writes clear, impactful tutorials.",
    verbose=True
)

crew = Crew(agents=[planner, writer], tasks=[research_task, write_task], process=Process.sequential)
result = crew.kickoff()

title: Enterprise GenAI Search & Real-Time NER Pipeline
summary: Large-scale search infrastructure serving 60K+ daily queries across 4 international markets, combining dense semantic search, fuzzy matching, and spaCy NER.
problem: Mobile app users frequently entered complex, unstructured financial search queries (e.g., 'refund from delta airlines last month over $200') which failed on keyword search, yielding empty results and chat escalation.
approach: Architected a hybrid search retrieval engine combining dense vector embeddings, fuzzy matching, and an asynchronous Named Entity Recognition (NER) pipeline (spaCy, NLTK, regex) to extract temporal entities, merchant names, and monetary values. Integrated Apache Kafka for event-driven telemetry and built Tableau performance dashboards.
architecture:
graph TD
    A[Mobile App Search: 60K+ req/day] --> B[Typeahead & Gateway API]
    B --> C{Query Parser}
    C --> D[NER Microservice: spaCy + Regex]
    C --> E[Dense Semantic Embeddings]
    C --> F[Fuzzy / Keyword Index]
    D & E & F --> G[Hybrid Score Fusion & Reranking]
    G --> H[Personalized Card Results & FAQ Synthesis]
    H --> I[Kafka Event Stream for Analytics]

metrics.label: Click-Through Rate (CTR)
metrics.delta: Measured across US, UK, AU, JP markets

metrics.label: Empty Query Resolution
metrics.delta: Successfully parsed via custom NER pipeline

title: AI-Powered Credit Risk & Decisioning Agentic Platform
summary: Stateful agentic decisioning system in LangGraph featuring memory persistence, SQLite checkpointing, MLflow evaluation, and ReactJS explainability dashboards.
problem: Commercial loan underwriting required manual aggregation of structured financial statements, credit bureau feeds, and qualitative disclosures, taking up to 72 hours per application with fragmented audit trails.
approach: Constructed a stateful agentic decisioning platform in LangGraph with memory persistence and checkpointing. Combined statistical risk models with LLM-based reasoning chains to generate standardized, regulatory-compliant risk profiles with full provenance tracking and MLflow monitoring.
architecture:
graph TD
    A[Loan Application Feed] --> B[FastAPI Gateway]
    B --> C[Data Aggregator: Bureau + Banking Statements]
    C --> D[Statistical ML Risk Scoring Model]
    D --> E[LangGraph Stateful Underwriting Agent]
    E --> F[Automated Compliance & Sanctions Check]
    F --> G[Explainability & Underwriter Memo Generator]
    G --> H[MLflow Governance & Alerting]
    G --> I[ReactJS Underwriter Cockpit]

metrics.label: Underwriting Cycle Time
metrics.delta: From days to automated preliminary memo in minutes

metrics.label: Audit Traceability
metrics.delta: Complete checkpoint history for regulatory review

challengesAndLearnings: Ensuring the system strictly adhered to fair lending regulations and explainability criteria was achieved by decoupling the mathematical scoring engine from the LLM narrative synthesizer, ensuring deterministic risk tiering.

codeSnippet.code:
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END

class UnderwritingState(dict):
    application_id: str
    financial_metrics: dict
    risk_score: float
    compliance_passed: bool
    decision_memo: str

workflow = StateGraph(UnderwritingState)
workflow.add_node("calculate_risk", compute_risk_features)
workflow.add_node("verify_compliance", check_regulatory_rules)
workflow.add_node("synthesize_memo", generate_underwriter_rationale)

workflow.set_entry_point("calculate_risk")
workflow.add_edge("calculate_risk", "verify_compliance")
workflow.add_edge("verify_compliance", "synthesize_memo")
workflow.add_edge("synthesize_memo", END)

app = workflow.compile(checkpointer=sqlite_memory_saver)
